# Wireframing and Prototyping

## Procedure
1. Establish the authorized card, target task, research evidence, uncertainty, prototype exit criteria, and disposition owner. Define the evidence threshold for revising, retiring, or handing the prototype to implementation; use approved product-owned storage and synthetic data.
2. Sketch the smallest end-to-end flow, including navigation, errors, empty states, and recovery. Choose fidelity based on the question, not the available design tool.
3. Build an interactive prototype only within explicit prototype authority. Label simulated behavior and excluded backend/security behavior; a prototype is not production-ready delivery.
4. Review feasibility with delivery owners and request task-based evaluation through VOC when human research is authorized. Record observations separately from predictions.
5. Revise the flow from evidence and return decisions, limitations, and the next test. At exit, mark the prototype `retained for further test`, `superseded`, or `handed off`; identify the canonical artifact, version, owner, and whether simulated behavior must be replaced before implementation. Production implementation still requires the authorized card's readiness gates.

## Completion Checks
The target question has observed evidence or an explicit gap; task paths and simulated states are identifiable. Do not upload proprietary prototypes to external design services without permission.

## Source
Original procedure informed by item 3 of [Talia Hartwell's UX skills article](https://uxplaybook.org/articles/top-skills-every-ux-designer-needs), accessed October 11, 2026. Tool preferences and informal tips are not mandatory project rules.
